name: 1793 Chain cent (Flowing Hair, chain reverse)
history:
Day 2: The 1793 Chain Cent

After the 1792 Mint Act, Philadelphia finally had a federal Mint. In March 1793 it delivered its first circulating coins — copper cents.

The reverse was a ring of linked chains, meant as unity. Plenty of people didn’t read it that way. Critics saw a bad omen for liberty — “Liberty in chains” — and within months the Mint swapped in a wreath.

That short run is why collectors still hunt this one.

name: 1793 Liberty Cap half cent (head left)
history:
Day 4: The 1793 half cent

Yes, America once made change for half a penny. The 1792 Coinage Act called for copper half cents alongside cents, and in 1793 the Philadelphia Mint struck the first ones.

Liberty faces left, with her cap over her shoulder; a berried wreath wraps HALF CENT on the back. Small coin, big first.

name: 1793 Wreath cent
history:
Day 3: The 1793 Wreath Cent

The Chain Cent barely cleared the door before the street talked back. Critics said Liberty looked “in a fright,” and that chain reverse wasn’t reading as unity.

So the Mint swapped the chain for a wreath — same Philadelphia shop, same year. Flowing Hair Liberty stays on the front; a leafy wreath takes the reverse. One of America’s first circulating redesigns.
